korean-k1-l1.title: Basic vowel sounds
korean-k1-l1.concept: Hangul na di Korean alphabet. Each syllable na one block. If na vowel alone, write **ㅇ** before am; e no get sound for di start: 아 na just “a”.
korean-k1-l1.example: 아 · 어 · 오 · 우 · 으 · 이 (a · eo · o · u · eu · i)

korean-k1-l2.title: Basic consonant sounds
korean-k1-l2.concept: Put consonant before vowel to make syllable block: **ㄱ + ㅏ = 가** (ga). Read di block from left go right.
korean-k1-l2.example: 가 · 나 · 다 · 마 · 바 · 사 · 하 (ga · na · da · ma · ba · sa · ha)

korean-k1-l3.title: First words
korean-k1-l3.concept: Join syllable blocks to make words. Read each block, then pronounce them together.

korean-k1-l5.title: More consonant sounds
korean-k1-l5.concept: ㄹ sound dey between “r” and “l”. ㅈ (j), ㅊ (ch, with air puff), ㅋ (k, with air puff), ㅌ (t, with air puff) and ㅍ (p, with air puff) complete di basic consonants.
korean-k1-l5.example: 라 · 자 · 차 · 카 · 타 · 파 (ra · ja · cha · ka · ta · pa)

korean-k1-l6.title: Double consonants
korean-k1-l6.concept: ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ, ㅆ and ㅉ na tense sounds: say them with tight throat and no air puff, like di first sound for “skate”.
korean-k1-l6.example: 까 · 따 · 빠 · 싸 · 짜 (kka · tta · ppa · ssa · jja)

korean-k1-l8.title: Words for everyday life
korean-k1-l8.concept: Read each word syllable by syllable. You dey read 학교 as “hakgyo”: close di final ㄱ for 학, then pronounce di next syllable with tense sound.

korean-k1-l9.title: Words about di world
korean-k1-l9.concept: People and nature: 사람 (person), 나라 (country), 하늘 (sky), 산 (mountain), 강 (river), 꽃 (flower).

korean-k2-l4.title: Polite expressions
korean-k2-l4.concept: Use 실례합니다 to get person attention or pass, 고마워요 to thank person in friendly way, 천만에요 to answer thanks, and 축하해요 to congratulate person.
korean-k2-l4.example: 실례합니다. (sillyehamnida.) = Excuse me. / 고마워요. (gomawoyo.) = Thank you. (friendly way)

korean-k2-l5.title: Names and countries
korean-k2-l5.concept: Ask name with 이름이 뭐예요? and country with 어느 나라 사람이에요? Answer with 제 이름은 ___예요 or 저는 ___ 사람이에요.
korean-k2-l5.example: 이름이 뭐예요? (ireumi mwoyeyo?) = Wetin be your name?

korean-k2-l6.title: How to talk goodbye
korean-k2-l6.concept: Among friends, you fit talk 잘 가요 (goodbye), 내일 봐요 (see you tomorrow), 또 만나요 (see you again) and 잘 자요 (sleep well).
korean-k2-l6.example: 잘 가요. (jal gayo.) = Goodbye. (friendly way) / 내일 봐요. (naeil bwayo.) = We go see tomorrow.

korean-k2-l7.title: How you dey?
korean-k2-l7.concept: Ask 잘 지냈어요? (You don dey well?) and answer 잘 지내요 (I dey well). 좋은 아침이에요 mean “Na good morning.”
korean-k2-l7.example: 잘 지내요. (jal jinaeyo.) = I dey well.

korean-k2-l8.title: Ask for help
korean-k2-l8.concept: Talk 도와주세요 to ask for help, 모르겠어요 when you no know, 알겠어요 when you understand, and 다시 말해 주세요 to ask person to talk am again.
korean-k2-l8.example: 도와주세요. (dowajuseyo.) = Abeg help me. / 알겠어요. (algesseoyo.) = I understand.

korean-k2-l9.title: Wetin you like and how to answer
korean-k2-l9.concept: 좋아요 mean good or fine, 싫어요 mean you no like am, 맞아요 mean “na correct” and 틀려요 mean “e no correct”.
korean-k2-l9.example: 좋아요. (joayo.) = E good. / 싫어요. (sireoyo.) = I no like am.

korean-k3-l4.title: Native Korean numbers 6–10
korean-k3-l4.concept: Continue di native Korean numbers: 여섯 (6), 일곱 (7), 여덟 (8), 아홉 (9), 열 (10).
korean-k3-l4.example: 여섯 · 일곱 · 여덟 · 아홉 · 열 (yeoseot · ilgop · yeodeol · ahop · yeol)

korean-k3-l5.title: Sino-Korean numbers
korean-k3-l5.concept: Sino-Korean numbers: 일 (1), 이 (2), 삼 (3), 사 (4), 오 (5), 육 (6), 칠 (7), 팔 (8), 구 (9), 십 (10). Dem dey use them for money, dates, phone numbers and minutes.
korean-k3-l5.example: 일 · 이 · 삼 · 사 · 오 · 육 · 칠 · 팔 · 구 · 십 (il · i · sam · sa · o · yuk · chil · pal · gu · sip)

korean-k3-l6.title: Age
korean-k3-l6.concept: Ask 몇 살이에요? (How old you be?). For age, use native numbers plus 살: 열 살 (10 years), 스무 살 (20), 서른 살 (30).
korean-k3-l6.example: 몇 살이에요? (myeot sarieyo?) = How old you be?

korean-k3-l8.title: More family words
korean-k3-l8.concept: For siblings, di word depend on who dey talk: woman dey call older brother 오빠 and older sister 언니. Also 아들 (son), 딸 (daughter), 부모님 (parents).
korean-k3-l8.example: 오빠 (oppa) = older brother (na woman dey talk am) / 언니 (eonni) = older sister (na woman dey talk am)

korean-k3-l9.title: Our family
korean-k3-l9.concept: Koreans often talk 우리 (we, our) instead of “my”: 우리 가족 mean “my family”. Count people with 명: 네 명 (four people).

korean-k4-l1.title: Everyday verbs
korean-k4-l1.concept: Polite present-tense verbs dey end with **-아요 / -어요 / -해요**. Di same form dey work for “I”, “you” and “they”.
korean-k4-l1.example: 먹어요. (meogeoyo.) = (I) dey chop. / 마셔요. (masyeoyo.) = (I) dey drink.

korean-k4-l4.title: Food and drink
korean-k4-l4.concept: 밥 (rice or food), 빵 (bread), 과일 (fruit), 고기 (meat), 물 (water), 우유 (milk).

korean-k4-l5.title: Wetin you like and no like
korean-k4-l5.concept: Use -를/을 좋아해요 to talk wetin you like and -를/을 싫어해요 for wetin you no like: 저는 사과를 좋아해요.

korean-k4-l6.title: Describe things
korean-k4-l6.concept: Describing words dey end with -요 too: 커요 (big), 작아요 (small), 많아요 (plenty), 맛있어요 (sweet to chop), 예뻐요 (fine).
korean-k4-l6.example: 커요. (keoyo.) = E big. / 작아요. (jagayo.) = E small.

korean-k4-l7.title: Weather
korean-k4-l7.concept: 날씨 (weather), 더워요 (e hot), 추워요 (e cold), 비가 와요 (rain dey fall), 눈이 와요 (snow dey fall).
korean-k4-l7.example: 더워요. (deowoyo.) = E hot. / 추워요. (chuwoyo.) = E cold.

korean-k4-l8.title: Make negative sentences with 안 and 못
korean-k4-l8.concept: Put **안** before verb to talk say you no do something (안 가요). Put **못** before am to talk say you no fit do am (못 가요).
korean-k4-l8.example: 안 먹어요. (an meogeoyo.) = I no dey chop.

korean-k4-l9.title: Wetin you dey do every day
korean-k4-l9.concept: 일어나요 (wake up), 씻어요 (wash), 일해요 (work), 자요 (sleep). Time words like 아침 (morning) and 밤 (night) dey take 에: 아침에.

korean-k5-l4.title: Days for di week
korean-k5-l4.concept: 월요일 (Mon), 화요일 (Tue), 수요일 (Wed), 목요일 (Thu), 금요일 (Fri), 토요일 (Sat), 일요일 (Sun).

korean-k5-l5.title: Months
korean-k5-l5.concept: For months, use Sino-Korean number plus 월: 일월 (January), 삼월 (March), 오월 (May), 칠월 (July), 구월 (September), 십이월 (December).

korean-k5-l6.title: Talk di hour
korean-k5-l6.concept: For hours, use native numbers plus 시: 한 시 (1:00), 두 시 (2:00), 세 시 (3:00), 열 시 (10:00). Ask 몇 시예요?
korean-k5-l6.example: 한 시 · 두 시 · 세 시 (han si · du si · se si)

korean-k5-l7.title: How often something dey happen
korean-k5-l7.concept: 매일 (every day), 자주 (often), 가끔 (sometimes), 항상 (always). Put them before di verb.

korean-k5-l8.title: More past tense
korean-k5-l8.concept: Past ending na -았/었어요: 했어요 (bin do), 왔어요 (bin come), 만났어요 (bin meet), 샀어요 (bin buy), 잤어요 (bin sleep).

korean-k5-l9.title: Birthdays and weekends
korean-k5-l9.concept: 생일 (birthday), 주말 (weekend), 선물 (gift). To ask, talk 생일이 언제예요?; to answer, talk 제 생일은 오월이에요.
korean-k5-l9.example: 생일이 언제예요? (saengiri eonjeyeyo?) = When be your birthday?

korean-k6-l4.title: For restaurant
korean-k6-l4.concept: 메뉴 (menu), 주문할게요 (I go order), 물 더 주세요 (more water, abeg), 계산해 주세요 (bring di bill, abeg).
korean-k6-l4.example: 계산해 주세요. (gyesanhae juseyo.) = Di bill, abeg.

korean-k6-l5.title: Move from place to place
korean-k6-l5.concept: 버스 (bus), 지하철 (underground train), 택시 (taxi), 기차 (train). Use -로/으로 to talk how you dey go: 버스로 가요.

korean-k6-l6.title: Phone calls and messages
korean-k6-l6.concept: 전화 (phone call), 전화번호 (phone number), 문자 (text message). 전화해요 mean “I dey call”.

korean-k6-l7.title: For hospital
korean-k6-l7.concept: 병원 (hospital), 약 (medicine), 아파요 (e dey pain). Talk di body part first: 머리가 아파요 (my head dey pain).
korean-k6-l7.example: 병원 (byeongwon) = hospital / 아파요. (apayo.) = E dey pain.

korean-k6-l8.title: Ask politely
korean-k6-l8.concept: -세요 and -아/어 주세요 dey make polite requests: 앉으세요 (abeg sit), 기다려 주세요 (abeg wait), 문을 열어 주세요 (abeg open di door).

korean-k6-l9.title: Make plans together
korean-k6-l9.concept: Use 같이 (together) to invite person: 같이 가요. 갈래요? dey ask “You wan go?” and 시간 있어요? dey ask “You get time?”
korean-k6-l9.example: 같이 가요. (gachi gayo.) = Make we go together.

korean-k7-l6.title: Report wetin person talk (-다고 하다)
korean-k7-l6.concept: Report wetin person dey talk or don talk: verb/adj + -다고 하다.
korean-k7-l6.example: 친구가 온다고 해요. (chinguga ondago haeyo.) = E say friend dey come.

korean-k7-l7.title: Report question (-냐고 하다)
korean-k7-l7.example: 어디 가냐고 물었어요. (eodi ganyago mureosseoyo.) = E ask where person dey go.

korean-k7-l8.title: Report commands and suggestions (-라고 / -자고 하다)
korean-k7-l8.concept: Report command (-라고 하다) or suggestion (-자고 하다).
korean-k7-l8.example: 빨리 오라고 했어요. (ppalli orago haesseoyo.) = E tell person make e come quick / 같이 가자고 했어요. (gachi gajago haesseoyo.) = E suggest make we go together

korean-k7-l9.title: Complex causes and contrasts (-느라고, -는데도)
korean-k7-l9.concept: Cause wey get negative result or delay (-느라고), and contrast despite di situation (-는데도).
korean-k7-l9.example: 공부하느라고 바빴어요. (gongbuhaneurago bapasseoyo.) = E busy dey study / 비가 오는데도 갔어요. (biga oneundedo gasseoyo.) = E go even though rain dey fall

korean-k7-l10.title: Proportion and wetin normally go happen (-을수록, -기 마련이다)
korean-k7-l10.concept: Di more... di more (-을수록), and wetin normally go happen (-기 마련이다).
korean-k7-l10.example: 만날수록 좋아요. (mannalsurok joayo.) = Di more di meetings, di better / 사람은 실수하기 마련이에요. (sarameun silsuhagi maryeonieyo.) = People bound to make mistakes

korean-k7-l11.title: How something look and wetin person fit infer (-아/어 보이다, -는 모양이다)
korean-k7-l11.concept: E look like (-아/어 보이다), and e appear say (-는 모양이다).
korean-k7-l11.example: 행복해 보여요. (haengbokae boyeoyo.) = E look happy / 비가 오는 모양이에요. (biga oneun moyangieyo.) = E be like rain dey fall

korean-k7-l12.title: Pretend (-는 척하다)
korean-k7-l12.concept: Make as if you dey do something or you be something: -(으)ㄴ/는 척하다.
korean-k7-l12.example: 아는 척해요. (aneun cheokaeyo.) = E dey pretend say e know

korean-k7-l13.title: Regret and wetin no happen (-(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬어요)
korean-k7-l13.concept: Express regret: 'I for don do...' -(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬어요.
korean-k7-l13.example: 일찍 올 걸 그랬어요. (iljjik ol geol geuraesseoyo.) = I for don come early

korean-k7-l14.title: K7 complete revision
korean-k7-l14.concept: Revise reported speech, complex connectors and expressions wey get small differences for meaning.
korean-k7-l14.example: 친구가 온다고 했어요. (chinguga ondago haesseoyo.) = E talk say friend dey come / 같이 밥 먹자고 했어요. (gachi bap meokjago haesseoyo.) = E suggest make we chop together

korean-k8-l1.title: Respectful words for di subject of sentence
korean-k8-l1.concept: Special respectful nouns and verbs for people wey you dey honour: 진지, 주무시다, 편찮으시다.
korean-k8-l1.example: 할머니께서 진지를 드세요. (halmeonikkeseo jinjireul deuseyo.) = Grandmama dey chop food

korean-k8-l2.title: Verbs wey show respect to di object (드리다, 뵙다, 여쭙다)
korean-k8-l2.concept: Humble/respectful verbs when action dey go toward elder: 드리다, 뵙다, 여쭙다.
korean-k8-l2.example: 선물을 드려요. (seonmureul deuryeoyo.) = Give gift respectfully / 내일 봬요. (naeil bwaeyo.) = See you tomorrow, with respect

korean-k8-l3.title: Passive forms with affixes (-이/히/리/기-)
korean-k8-l3.concept: Add -이/히/리/기- to form passive verbs: 보이다, 들리다, 열리다, 닫히다.
korean-k8-l3.example: 문이 열려요. (muni yeollyeoyo.) = Di door dey open / 창문이 닫혀요. (changmuni dachyeoyo.) = Di window dey close

korean-k8-l4.title: Passive expressions (-어지다, -게 되다)
korean-k8-l4.concept: Verbs wey show spontaneous or resulting passive forms: -아/어지다, -게 되다.
korean-k8-l4.example: 글씨가 써져요. (geulssiga sseojyeoyo.) = Di writing dey come out / 알게 되었어요. (alge doeeosseoyo.) = E come know

korean-k8-l5.title: Causative forms with affixes (-이/히/리/기/우-)
korean-k8-l5.concept: Causative verbs wey make person do action: 보여 주다, 먹이다, 입히다.
korean-k8-l5.example: 사진을 보여 줘요. (sajineul boyeo jwoyo.) = E dey show photo / 아기에게 밥을 먹여요. (agiege babeul meogyeoyo.) = E dey feed baby

korean-k8-l6.title: Causative expressions (-게 하다)
korean-k8-l6.concept: Make or cause person to do something: -게 하다.
korean-k8-l6.example: 웃게 해요. (utge haeyo.) = E dey make person laugh / 기다리게 했어요. (gidarige haesseoyo.) = E make person wait

korean-k8-l7.title: Formal public style (-하십시오)
korean-k8-l7.concept: Very formal respectful style for announcements and ceremonies: -하십시오, -하십시다.
korean-k8-l7.example: 자리에 앉으십시오. (jarie anjeusipsio.) = Abeg take your seat / 출발하십시다. (chulbalhasipsida.) = Make we depart

korean-k8-l8.title: Modest expressions wey lower yourself politely
korean-k8-l8.concept: Polite speech wey use humble pronouns and verbs: 저희, 말씀 올리다.
korean-k8-l8.example: 인사 말씀 올립니다. (insa malsseum ollimnida.) = I dey offer greeting words respectfully / 저희 학교입니다. (jeohui hakgyoimnida.) = Na our school, said humbly

korean-k8-l9.title: K8 complete revision
korean-k8-l9.concept: Revise respectful forms, passive, causative and formal polite styles.
korean-k8-l9.example: 할머니께 선물을 드렸어요. (halmeonikke seonmureul deuryeosseoyo.) = Grandmama don receive gift / 문이 저절로 닫혔어요. (muni jeojeollo dachyeosseoyo.) = Di door close by itself

korean-k9-l1.title: Write work emails and make requests
korean-k9-l1.concept: Formal work email expressions: -에 관하여, 검토 부탁드립니다.
korean-k9-l1.example: 회의 안건에 관하여 말씀드립니다. (hoeui angeone gwanhayeo malsseumdeurimnida.) = I dey talk respectfully about di meeting agenda

korean-k9-l2.title: Good manners for work phone calls
korean-k9-l2.concept: Handle calls and messages: 통화 가능하신지요, 연결해 드리겠습니다.
korean-k9-l2.example: 지금 통화 가능하신지요? (jigeum tonghwa ganeunghasinjiyo?) = You fit talk now? / 담당자를 연결해 드리겠습니다. (damdangjareul yeongyeolhae deurigetseumnida.) = I go connect you to di person in charge

korean-k9-l3.title: Arrange and change schedules
korean-k9-l3.concept: Suggest and change appointment time: 변경하고자 합니다, 양해 부탁드립니다.
korean-k9-l3.example: 일정을 변경하고자 합니다. (iljeongeul byeongyeonghagoja hamnida.) = I wan change di schedule / 너른 양해 부탁드립니다. (neoreun yanghae butakdeurimnida.) = Abeg make you understand

korean-k9-l4.title: Talk and give opinion for meetings
korean-k9-l4.concept: Give views for meetings: 제 생각으로는, 찬성합니다, 추가 검토.
korean-k9-l4.example: 제 생각으로는 이번 안이 좋습니다. (je saenggakeoroneun ibeon ani jotseumnida.) = As I see am, this proposal good / 적극 찬성합니다. (jeokgeuk chanseonghamnida.) = I strongly agree

korean-k9-l5.title: Report how project dey go
korean-k9-l5.concept: Give progress reports: 진행 상황을 보고합니다, 조치를 완료했습니다.
korean-k9-l5.example: 프로젝트 진행 상황을 보고합니다. (peurojekteu jinhaeng sanghwangeul bogohamnida.) = I dey report how di project dey go / 조치를 완료했습니다. (jochireul wallyohaesseumnida.) = Di action don finish

korean-k9-l6.title: Statistics and how data dey change
korean-k9-l6.concept: Describe trends and numbers: 증가했습니다, 전년 대비.
korean-k9-l6.example: 매출이 증가했습니다. (maechuri jeunggahaesseumnida.) = Sales don increase / 전년 대비 상승했습니다. (jeonnyeon daebi sangseunghaesseumnida.) = E rise compared with last year

korean-k9-l7.title: Business negotiations and partnerships
korean-k9-l7.concept: Work together professionally: 상호 협력을 희망합니다, 절충안 제시.
korean-k9-l7.example: 상호 협력을 희망합니다. (sangho hyeomnyeogeul huimanghamnida.) = We hope to work together / 절충안을 제안합니다. (jeolchuganeul jeanhamnida.) = I propose compromise

korean-k9-l8.title: Business cards and work titles
korean-k9-l8.concept: Exchange business cards and titles: 처음 뵙겠습니다, 명함 드립니다.
korean-k9-l8.example: 처음 뵙겠습니다, 명함 드립니다. (cheoeum boepgetseumnida, myeongham deurimnida.) = E good to meet you; na my business card be this / 김 부장님입니다. (gim bujangnimimnida.) = Na department manager Kim

korean-k9-l9.title: K9 complete revision
korean-k9-l9.concept: Revise professional communication, formal letters and meetings.
korean-k9-l9.example: 안건을 검토해 주시기 바랍니다. (angeoneul geomtohae jusigi baramnida.) = Abeg review di agenda / 회의에서 뵙겠습니다. (hoeuieseo boepgetseumnida.) = We go see for di meeting

korean-k10-l1.title: Headlines and shortened writing style
korean-k10-l1.concept: News headlines and shortened noun phrases: 물가 안정 대책 발표.
korean-k10-l1.example: 물가 안정 대책을 발표했습니다. (mulga anjeong daechaegeul balpyohaesseumnida.) = Measures to stabilise prices don get announced

korean-k10-l2.title: Current affairs and editorials
korean-k10-l2.concept: Read short news reports: 친환경 에너지가 주목받고 있습니다.
korean-k10-l2.example: 친환경 에너지가 주목받고 있습니다. (chinhwan-gyeong eneojiga jumokbatgo isseumnida.) = Environment-friendly energy dey get attention

korean-k10-l3.title: Body-part idioms (발, 눈, 귀, 손)
korean-k10-l3.concept: Common body-part idioms: 발이 넓다 (know plenty people), 눈이 높다 (get high standards).
korean-k10-l3.example: 김 대리는 발이 넓어요. (gim daerineun bari neobeoyo.) = Assistant manager Kim know plenty people / 눈이 높아요. (nuni nopayo.) = E get high standards

korean-k10-l4.title: Everyday action idioms (바가지, 어깨)
korean-k10-l4.concept: Expressions for common situations: 바가지를 쓰다 (pay too much because person cheat you), 어깨가 무겁다 (get heavy responsibility).
korean-k10-l4.example: 바가지를 썼어요. (bagajireul sseosseoyo.) = Person overcharge me / 어깨가 무거워요. (eokkaega mugeowoyo.) = Di responsibility heavy for me

korean-k10-l5.title: Important Korean proverbs
korean-k10-l5.concept: Wisdom inside proverbs: 소 잃고 외양간 고친다, 쇠뿔도 단김에 빼라.
korean-k10-l5.example: 소 잃고 외양간 고친다. (so ilko oeyanggan gochinda.) = Repair cowshed after cow don lost / 쇠뿔도 단김에 빼라. (soeppuldo dangime ppaera.) = Act while di chance still dey

korean-k10-l6.title: Four-character idioms (사자성어)
korean-k10-l6.concept: Common four-character idioms wey come from Chinese: 일석이조, 작심삼일, 다다익선.
korean-k10-l6.example: 일석이조예요. (ilseogijoyeyo.) = One action, two benefits / 작심삼일이에요. (jaksimsamirieyo.) = Resolve wey last only three days

korean-k10-l7.title: Words wey connect reasoning and guide discourse
korean-k10-l7.concept: Formal words wey guide discourse: -에 따르면, 한편, 요컨대, 따라서.
korean-k10-l7.example: 의견에 따르면 그렇습니다. (uigyone ttareumyeon geureotsseumnida.) = According to di opinion, na so e be / 한편 다른 측면도 있습니다. (hanpyeon dareun cheungmyeondo isseumnida.) = On di other hand, another side still dey

korean-k10-l8.title: Korean cultural values and customs in depth
korean-k10-l8.concept: Cultural ideas and holiday traditions: 따뜻한 정, 송편을 빚다.
korean-k10-l8.example: 따뜻한 정이 있어요. (ttatteutan jeongi isseoyo.) = Warm affection dey / 송편을 빚어요. (songpyeoneul bijeoyo.) = Make songpyeon rice cakes

korean-k10-l9.title: K10 complete revision
korean-k10-l9.concept: Understand Korean culture, media, idioms and formal debate expressions well.
korean-k10-l9.example: 일석이조의 효과를 거두었어요. (ilseogijoui hyogwareul geoduosseoyo.) = One action don bring two benefits / 상호 이해를 바탕으로 협력해요. (sangho ihaereul batangeuro hyeomnyeokaeyo.) = Work together based on mutual understanding

korean-k1-l4.title: Y-vowels
korean-k1-l4.concept: If you add one short stroke, e dey make **y** sound: ㅏ → ㅑ (ya), ㅓ → ㅕ (yeo), ㅗ → ㅛ (yo), ㅜ → ㅠ (yu). ㅐ (ae) and ㅔ (e) dey sound very similar for modern Korean.
korean-k1-l4.example: 야 · 여 · 요 · 유 (ya · yeo · yo · yu)

korean-k1-l7.title: Final consonants
korean-k1-l7.concept: Consonant wey dey under di syllable na **받침 (batchim)**. E dey close di syllable: 안 (an), 말 (mal), 밤 (bam), 강 (gang), 집 (jip), 책 (chaek). Only seven final sounds dey possible: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅇ.
korean-k1-l7.example: 안 · 말 · 밤 · 강 · 집 (an · mal · bam · gang · jip)

korean-k2-l1.title: Hello and thank you
korean-k2-l1.concept: Polite greetings dey end with **-요** or **-니다**. You fit use 안녕하세요 any time of day.

korean-k2-l2.title: Yes, no and okay
korean-k2-l2.concept: Short polite answers wey you fit use every day. Korean dey add **요** for di end to show politeness.

korean-k2-l3.title: Nice to meet you
korean-k2-l3.concept: When you meet new person, say 만나서 반갑습니다. Two ways dey to say goodbye: one for di person wey dey go, one for di person wey dey stay.
korean-k2-l3.example: 만나서 반갑습니다. (mannaseo bangapseumnida.) = E good to meet you.

korean-k2-l10.title: Signs wey you go see
korean-k2-l10.concept: Short signs dey everywhere for Korea. **입구** na entrance, **출구** na exit and **화장실** na toilet. For door, **미세요** mean push and **당기세요** mean pull.

korean-k2-l11.title: Thank you for di food
korean-k2-l11.concept: Before food, talk **잘 먹겠습니다**; when you finish, talk **잘 먹었습니다**. Person wey welcome you dey talk **어서 오세요**; **맛있어요** dey praise di food.
korean-k2-l11.example: 잘 먹겠습니다. (jal meokgetseumnida.) = Before you chop: “I go chop well.” / 잘 먹었습니다. (jal meogeotseumnida.) = After you chop: “I don chop well.”

korean-k3-l1.title: I be student
korean-k3-l1.concept: **저는** mean “I” in polite way. Put **이에요** after consonant and **예요** after vowel to say “I be …”.
korean-k3-l1.example: 저는 학생이에요. (jeoneun haksaengieyo.) = I be student.

korean-k3-l2.title: My family
korean-k3-l2.concept: People dey use family words plenty for Korean, even for people wey no be family.

korean-k3-l3.title: Count numbers
korean-k3-l3.concept: Korean get two number systems: native Korean (하나, 둘, 셋 …) for counting things, and Sino-Korean (일, 이, 삼 …) for money, dates and minutes.

korean-k3-l10.title: Send message to friend
korean-k3-l10.concept: Text messages dey use short polite sentences wey end with **-요**. **지금 어디예요?** dey ask where you dey, **곧 가요** mean “I dey come soon” and **늦어요** mean “I dey late”.
korean-k3-l10.example: 지금 어디예요? (jigeum eodiyeyo?) = Where you dey now? / 곧 가요. (got gayo.) = I dey come soon.

korean-k3-l11.title: Read words loud
korean-k3-l11.concept: When syllable end with consonant and di next one start with vowel, di sound dey move over: 책이 sound like **chaegi** and 밥을 like **babeul**. Some sounds dey change their neighbours too: 국물 sound like **gungmul**, 같이 like **gachi**.

korean-k4-l2.title: Go places
korean-k4-l2.concept: Put **에** after place to show where you dey go or come: 학교에 가요. Di verb dey come last.
korean-k4-l2.example: 학교에 가요. (hakgyoe gayo.) = I dey go school.

korean-k4-l3.title: Chop, drink and read
korean-k4-l3.concept: Di object of verb dey take **을** after consonant and **를** after vowel: 밥을 먹어요, 커피를 마셔요.
korean-k4-l3.example: 밥을 먹어요. (babeul meogeoyo.) = I dey chop food.

korean-k5-l1.title: Yesterday, today and tomorrow
korean-k5-l1.concept: Time words normally dey near di start of sentence.

korean-k5-l2.title: Wetin I don do
korean-k5-l2.concept: Past tense: **-았어요 / -었어요 / -했어요**. Some verbs dey shorten: 가다 → 갔어요, 보다 → 봤어요.

korean-k5-l3.title: Wetin I go do
korean-k5-l3.concept: Use **-(으)ㄹ 거예요** to talk your plans: 가다 → 갈 거예요, 먹다 → 먹을 거예요.
korean-k5-l3.example: 내일 갈 거예요. (naeil gal geoyeyo.) = I go go tomorrow.

korean-k6-l1.title: For shop
korean-k6-l1.concept: Ask price with 얼마예요? and use **… 주세요** (… abeg) to ask for something.

korean-k6-l2.title: Where e dey?
korean-k6-l2.concept: Ask **… 어디예요?** (Where … dey?). Listen for 오른쪽 (right), 왼쪽 (left) and 직진 (straight).
korean-k6-l2.example: 화장실이 어디예요? (hwajangsiri eodiyeyo?) = Where toilet dey?

korean-k6-l3.title: I wan …
korean-k6-l3.concept: Add **-고 싶어요** to verb stem to talk wetin you wan do: 가다 → 가고 싶어요.
korean-k6-l3.example: 가고 싶어요. (gago sipeoyo.) = I wan go.

korean-k7-l1.title: Endings wey show politeness for formal talk
korean-k7-l1.concept: For formal speech and work, add -ㅂ니다 to verb or adjective stem wey end with vowel, and -습니다 to stem wey end with consonant. Questions dey end with -ㅂ니까 / -습니까.
korean-k7-l1.example: 저는 학생입니다. (jeoneun haksaengimnida.) = I be student. / 이름이 무엇입니까? (ireumi mueosimnikka?) = Wetin be your name?

korean-k7-l2.title: Di basic forms for plain written statements
korean-k7-l2.concept: Plain written style dey end statements with -ㄴ다 / -는다 and past statements with -았다 / -었다. These forms na di base for reported speech for di next lessons.
korean-k7-l2.example: 나는 학교에 간다. (naneun hakgyoe ganda.) = I dey go school. / 동생은 책을 읽는다. (dongsaengeun chaegeul ingneunda.) = My younger broda or sista dey read book.

korean-k7-l3.title: Describe nouns
korean-k7-l3.concept: Verb or adjective fit describe noun: put -(으)ㄴ for adjectives and past actions, -는 for present actions, and -(으)ㄹ for future or planned actions before di noun.
korean-k7-l3.example: 저는 맛있는 음식을 좋아해요. (jeoneun masinneun eumsigeul joahaeyo.) = I like food wey sweet. / 예쁜 꽃을 샀어요. (yeppeun kkocheul sasseoyo.) = I don buy fine flowers.

korean-k7-l4.title: Basic words wey join ideas
korean-k7-l4.concept: Join two clauses with -아/어서 (reason or sequence), -지만 (contrast), -(으)니까 (reason), -(으)면 (if) and -(으)려고 (to show purpose).
korean-k7-l4.example: 피곤해서 일찍 잤어요. (pigonhaeseo iljjik jasseoyo.) = I tire, so I sleep early. / 비가 와서 집에 있었어요. (biga waseo jibe isseosseoyo.) = Rain fall, so I stay house.

korean-k7-l5.title: Wetin person fit do, wetin person must do, and wetin person get permission to do
korean-k7-l5.concept: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 dey express ability or possibility, -아/어야 하다 obligation, and -아/어도 되다 permission.
korean-k7-l5.example: 저는 수영할 수 있어요. (jeoneun suyeonghal su isseoyo.) = I fit swim. / 저는 한국어로 이야기할 수 있어요. (jeoneun hangugeoro iyagihal su isseoyo.) = I fit talk Korean.
